quiz.q: Why was Panchayati Raj initially placed under Directive Principles (Article 40) rather than made an enforceable right?
options: Modernists favored a centralized federation and state-led development over Gandhian democratic decentralization.
Gandhian leaders opposed grassroots democracy, demanding that all administrative power remain with New Delhi.
The Drafting Committee intended local self-government institutions to handle only urban municipal administration.
External donor agencies required post-independence India to abolish village councils before receiving financial assistance.
quiz.why: Modernists like Nehru and Ambedkar favored centralized planning and federation, prevailing over the Gandhian school's demand for decentralized village self-rule.

quiz.q: Why did Panchayati Raj institutions suffer widespread stagnation during the 1970s and 1980s?
options: The Supreme Court declared the Balvantray Mehta three-tier framework unconstitutional across all Indian states.
State political leaders and hostile bureaucrats resisted sharing power and resources with emerging local representatives.
Rural communities rejected local councils because land reforms had already eliminated caste and class dominance.
The Union government transferred all rural development subjects directly into the exclusive Union Legislative List.
quiz.why: State leaders feared losing authority to emerging grassroots leaders, while a hostile bureaucracy resisted surrendering power and resources.

quiz.q: Why do scholars characterize the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act as a 'half-baked cake'?
options: It made regular five-year elections and social auditing entirely optional for all state governments.
It omitted reservations for marginalized communities and women in rural local self-government institutions.
It created an institutional skeleton while leaving actual devolution of subjects to state legislative discretion.
It abolished village-level panchayats in favor of centralized planning commissions at the national level.
quiz.why: While the amendment created a mandatory three-tier structure, it left the transfer of funds, functions, and functionaries to the discretion of individual states.

quiz.q: What is a major institutional weakness of the Gram Sabha under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act?
options: The amendment mandates direct elections for village representatives but prohibits villagers from gathering in assemblies.
Its membership is restricted only to village elders and landowners rather than all adult registered voters.
State governments are constitutionally barred from conducting any meetings of the Gram Sabha during peacetime.
The amendment fails to clearly define the specific powers, functions, and role of the Gram Sabha.
quiz.why: Unlike the PESA Act, the 73rd Amendment left the powers and functions of the Gram Sabha largely undefined, weakening its oversight role.
